Sir,
    In a report published in the Shanghai Min Kuo Jih Pao,
a Kuomintang organ, January 9 issue, regarding the attempted
assassination of the Japanese Emperor in Tokyo on January 8,
there appeared a quotation referring to the incident which is
calculated by Japanese to be an insult to the Emperor of Japan,
and which has aroused their indignation, and has formed the subject of
protests in the form of Notes forwarded to Mr. Wu Tieh Cheng,
Mayor of Shanghai, by Mr. Karamatsu Murai, Japanese Consul
General in Shanghai, bringing the article in question to the
notice of the former with a view to having a correction and
apology inserted in the newspaper in question by the publishers.
In reply Mr. Wu Tieh Cheng tendered an apology to Mr. K. Murai
and stated that he had duly notified the Editor of the Min Kuo
Jih Pao of the contents of the note. Subsequently on January 12,
the Min Kuo Jih Pao published the text of a Note from the
Japanese Consul General to the Mayor of Greater Shanghai
referring to the article published in the Min Kuo Jih Pao as
being an insult to the Japanese Emperor and Japan, and requesting
a correction and apology be published, and punishment be meted
out to the persons responsible for the publication.
    Together with the above the editor of the Min Kuo Jih
Pao published a note referring to the note from the Japanese
Consul General and giving his interpretation of the offensive
article referred to in the letter, and stating that no offence
or insult to the Japanese Emperor was intended, but on the
contrary it expressed regret at the incident. He also stated
that owing to lack of full knowledge of the Chinese language
the Japanese Consular Officials had misconstrued the article.

先生，
    在上海《民国日报》（国民党机关报）1月9日刊出的一篇关于1月8日发生在东京的刺杀日本天皇未遂事件的报道中，出现了一段引文。日本人认为这段引文是对日本天皇的侮辱，激起了他们的愤慨，并以此为由提出抗议。日本驻上海总领事村井乾松（Karamatsu Murai）先生向上海市市长吴铁城先生递交了照会，提请前者注意该文章，旨在要求报社在该报上刊登更正及道歉声明。作为回复，吴铁城先生向村井乾松先生表示歉意，并称已适当通知《民国日报》编辑有关照会的内容。随后在1月12日，《民国日报》刊登了日本驻上海总领事致大上海市市长的照会全文，称《民国日报》刊登的文章是对日本天皇及日本的侮辱，并要求刊登更正及道歉声明，并对负责出版的人员予以惩处。

    与此同时，《民国日报》编辑发表了一份说明，提及日本总领事的照会，并对信中提到的冒犯性文章进行了解释，声明并无冒犯或侮辱日本天皇之意，相反，对该事件表示了遗憾。他还声称，由于日本领事官员中文知识不全，误解了该文章。

The quotation referred to in the article published in

Negations in the Chinese written language being so

ordered in this cunning way in order to give a wrong impression

**JAPANESE CONSUL MISAPPREHENDS THE HEADING OF OUR PAPER.**

The Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai
yesterday sent the following letter to the Municipality
of Greater Shanghai:-

"On January 9 the Min Kuo Pao published an
article bearing on an incident which occurred in Tokyo on
January 8, and beneath the heading "Attempted Assassination
of Japanese Emperor by a Korean", the paper inserted a small
heading "It is unfortunate that the carriage following the
Emperor was bombed and that the culprit was at once arrested".

"This Consulate General considers the expression
as insulting to the Emp ror of my country and that the Min
Kuo Pao has deliberately aroused the indignation of Japanese.
I request that the paper concerned be instructed immediately
to make a correction, to publish an apology and to punish the
responsible persons of the paper. Simultaneously, I request
that ways and means be devised to put a stop to future
appearance in all local Chinese papers of articles of this
nature.

* I shall be much obliged if you will favor me with
a reply stating the result of your action in this connection".

日本驻上海总领事昨日致函大上海市政府：

“本总领事馆认为该表述是对我国天皇的侮辱，且《民国报》故意激起日本人的愤慨。我要求立即指令相关报社进行更正，刊登道歉声明，并惩处报社责任人。同时，我要求设法制止今后所有本地中文报纸再出现此类性质的文章。

~~备注~~ 按语：

~~本报已收到~~ 鉴于上述情况，本报收到大上海市政府转来的日本总领事馆照会内容。鉴于两个邻邦之间的友好关系，我们中国人应当对日本天皇遇刺未遂一事表达适当的情感。标题“不幸跟随天皇的车厢被炸，凶手当即被捕”的含义是基于此

sentiment. The bombing of the carriage following the
Emperor's is not a pleasant affair and consequently it is
said to be unfortunate. Had the Japanese Emperor been
bombed, the word "unfortunate" would not have been adequate
to describe the case. This paper had no intention of
insulting the Emperor of Japan, on the contrary expressed
a slight expression of regret in the article in question.
This article must have been misapprehended or misinterpreted
by the staff of the Japanese Consulate who only know part of
the Chinese language and this has resulted in the demands
from the Japanese Consul-General. For this reason, we
do not know how to make the correction and as to the demands
for apology and punishment, it is absolutely unreasonable.
The Chinese have so far never committed any improper acts
in newspapers in the Orient to exasperate the feelings of
people of foreign countries. There are newspapers in
the world which are deliberately arousing the indignation
of the Chinese authorities. We regret this matter very
much. We tender appropriate thanks to the Japanese Consul-
General for his manner of action.

种情感。跟随天皇的车厢被炸并非令人愉快之事，因此称之为“不幸”。如果日本天皇被炸，“不幸”一词将不足以形容该情况。本报无意侮辱日本天皇，相反，在上述文章中表达了轻微的遗憾之意。该文章必定是被只懂部分中文的日本领事馆工作人员误解或曲解，从而导致了日本总领事的要求。基于此原因，我们不知如何进行更正，至于道歉和惩罚的要求，则是完全无理的。迄今为止，中国人在东方的报纸上从未做过任何激怒外国人士感情的不当行为。世界上有些报纸故意激起中国当局的愤慨。我们对此事深感遗憾。我们对日本总领事的行事方式表示适当的感谢。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JANUARY 18, 1932

Japanese Continue Agitation
For Min Kuo Jih Pao Apology

Minister Sends Note Of Protest About Three
Papers' Reports Of Assassination Attempt

SHANGHAI, Jan. 18.—A committee of local Nipponese residents called upon Consul-General Murai Saturday morning at the Consulate-General and submitted to him a copy of the resolution adopted last evening at an extraordinary meeting of the representatives of the Amalgamated Association of Street Unions, in connection with the indiscreet headlines and comments which appeared in the Min Kuo Jih Pao, a Kuomintang organ, a few days ago.

Apologies for the disrespectful editorial comments regarding the Japanese sovereign are demanded of the Chinese mayor of Shanghai, as well as of the editor of the Kuomintang paper. In addition, the local residents ask that punishment of some kind be administered to the paper, and that definite assurances be given that similar incidents will never be staged in the future.

If the Chinese refuse to apologize and comply with other Japanese requests, the local residents intend to call a mass meeting to discuss other ways of securing a satisfactory solution of the matter.

Branding the editorial headlines and comments appearing in the Min Kuo Jih Pao of Shanghai, that of Tsingtao, and that of Foochow as a "serious insult" to the Japanese Imperial Family and the Japanese nation, the Japanese minister to China in a note of protest under date of January 15, filed with the Waichiaopu, requests the national government to take speedy and appropriate steps for an early solution of the incident and for an effective control of these and other similar manifestations or expressions of anti-Japanese feelings on the part of the Chinese.

日本居民要求上海中国市长以及该国民党报纸的编辑就有关日本君主的不敬社论评论道歉。此外，当地居民要求对该报施加某种形式的惩罚，并给出明确保证，确保将来不再上演类似事件。

Set - Back Causes
Kuomintang Body

Tsingtao Tangpu Closes

Japanese Attack

TSINGTAO, Jan. 17.—(Special).—
The members of the local Kuomin-
tang headquarters at an urgent
meeting today decided to close the
office temporarily as it is impossible
to find quarters to carry on Party
work after the burning down of
their office by the Japanese resi-
dents in retaliation for alleged dis-
respect shown to their Emperor in
connection with the publication of
the news concerning the attempt
made on his life recently.

All the staff officers of the Kuo-
mintang headquarters here were
paid off and were informed that
their services might be required
later. The Kuo Min Jih Pao, the
organ of the Kuomintang at Tsing-
tao, is unable to resume publica-
tion indefinitely, as the damage
done by the Japanese to its print-
ing equipment was considerable.

Tsingtao Consul
Fulfills Demands
Of City Officials

TSINGTAO, Jan. 17.—(Kuomin).
—It is learned that the Japanese
Consul at Tsingtao has accepted the
demands of the Chinese authori-
ties in connection with the recent
outrages committed by Japanese
mobs on the premises of the "Min
Kuo Jih Pao", official Party organ,
and the Tsingtao Municipal Party
Headquarters.

The demands, it may be recalled,
include official apologies, indemnity
for damages done, punishment of
the ringleaders of the outrages, and
guarantees that there will be no
recurrence of similar incidents.

As a result of the complete de-
struction of their Headquarters as
well as all documents contained
therein, the Executive Committee
of the Municipal Party Headquar-
ters, at a meeting yesterday, decid-
ed to suspend Party activities for
the present.

国民党机构

青岛党部遭日本人袭击后
关闭办公地点

青岛，1月17日电。（特约）。— 当地国民党总部成员在今日的紧急会议上决定暂时关闭办公室，因为在日本居民为报复近期出版的关于刺杀天皇未遂新闻中据称对其天皇表现出的不敬而烧毁其办公室后，已无法找到场所开展党务工作。

此处国民党总部的所有职员均已结清薪资，并被告知日后可能需要他们的服务。青岛的国民党机关报《民国日报》无限期无法恢复出版，因为日本人对该报印刷设备造成的损坏相当严重。

由于其总部及其中所有文件被彻底摧毁，市党部执行委员会在昨日的会议上决定暂时停止党务活动。

PRESS UNION BULLETIN NO. 82

LOCAL JAPANESE BODIES WANT APOLOGY FROM MINKUO JIHPAO & MAYOR
Shanghai, Jan. 15.

Representatives of the Shanghai Japanese Associa-
tion of Street Unions are meeting this evening to discuss what
concrete measures should be adopted to secure definite apologies
from the Chinese Mayor of this city and also from the respon-
sible persons of the Minkuo Jihpao for the indiscreet head-
lines and the subsequent editorial comments insulting the Japanese
sovereign and the Japanese nation. These men also want assurances
from the Chinese that similar cases of affront to the Japanese
will never be staged, besides punishment for the responsible
persons for the recent incident.

Although Consul-General K. Murai has twice filed
Notes of protest with Mayor Wu Tieh-cheng of Greater Shanghai,
the latter has so far made no reply which will satisfy the
Japanese. Instead, the Mayor's first reply is considered
"insincere" by the Japanese, while the Minkuo Jihpao has even
published comments insulting the officials of the Japanese
Consulate-General, making no attempt whatever to apologize for
the disrespect shown to the Japanese sovereign.

Local Japanese residents think that diplomatic protests
when filed with Chinese officials are exceedingly ineffective,
judged from past experiences, and that something more effective
should be resorted to/stop the Chinese from continuing to
insult the Japanese. A mass meeting of the local Japanese
residents might be held shortly to voice a popular protest
against the Minkuo Jihpao and Mayor Wu and also to bring
pressure on the consular and diplomatic officials here to secure
better results.

当地日本团体要求《民国日报》及市长道歉
上海，1月15日。

上海日本街道工会联合会的代表今晚开会，讨论应采取何种具体措施，以确保本市中国市长以及《民国日报》负责人就侮辱日本君主和日本民族的不慎标题及随后的社论评论作出明确道歉。这些人还希望中方保证，除了惩罚近期事件的责任人外，绝不再上演类似冒犯日本人的案件。

尽管村井 K. Murai 总领事已两次向大上海市长吴铁城提交抗议照会，但后者至今未作出令日本人满意的答复。相反，日方认为市长的首次答复“缺乏诚意”，而《民国日报》甚至刊登了侮辱日本总领事馆官员的评论，完全没有试图为对日本君主表现出的不敬行为道歉。

当地日本居民认为，根据过去的经验，向中国官员提交的外交抗议极其无效，应该采取更有效的措施来阻止中国人继续侮辱日本人。不久可能会举行当地日本居民群众大会，表达对《民国日报》和吴市长的公众抗议，并向这里的领事和外交官员施加压力，以取得更好的结果。

Bulletin issued by the Japanese Press Union,

CHINESE PAPER ARROGANT: JAPANESE CONSUL-GENERAL TO PROTEST
AGAIN

Shanghai, Jan. 12.

Consul-General K. Murai, of Shanghai, is
expected shortly to despatch another Note of warning to Mayor
Wu Tieh-cheng, of Greater Shanghai, in connection with
the indiscreet and disrespectful headline which appeared
in the Jan. 9 issue of the Minkuo Jihpao, a local ver-
nacular and a well known Kuomintang organ.

Although Mayor Wu, in reply to Consul-General
Murai's first Note, issued on Jan. 10, stated that he
was sorry for the incident and that he had duly notified
the editor of the Minkuo Jihpao regarding the contents of
the Note, the paper in this morning's issue says that
no disrespect to the Japanese Emperor was intended. It
even goes on to say that the officials of the Japanese Con-
sulate-General in Shanghai fail to possess an adequate
reading knowledge of the Chinese language, and concludes
that there is no need of making any corrections in the
headline in question or offering any apology.

This arrogant attitude assumed by the paper
has again aroused the indignation of the officials of
the local Japanese Consulate-General, as well as the
Japanese community here. Consul-General Murai accordingly
expects to send another Note to Mayor Wu shortly.

The Minkuo Jihpao's headlines read:

（批：I.O. 8632/8^A.） "Korean Assassin Makes Attempt at Life of Japanese
Emperor; UNFORTUNATELY Bomb Explodes at Another
Carriage; Korean Captured on Spot".

This, it is pointed out, constitutes a deliberate
attempt on the part of the editor to insult the Japanese
sovereign and the Japanese nation. ---Press Union

1932年1月12日《民国报》刊登文章的译文。

日本领事误解本报标题

驻上海日本总领事昨日致函大上海市政府，内容如下：

“1月9日，《民国报》刊登了一篇关于1月8日发生在东京的事件的文章，并在‘朝鲜人企图刺杀日本天皇’的大标题下，插入了一行小标题：‘不幸皇帝随后的车厢被炸，罪犯随即被捕’。

“本总领事馆认为该表述是对我国天皇的侮辱，且《民国报》故意激起日本人的愤慨。我要求立即指令有关报纸进行更正，刊登道歉声明，并惩处该报责任人。同时，我要求制定办法，制止今后所有本地中文报纸再出现此类性质的文章。

“如蒙惠复告知贵方就此采取的行动结果，我将不胜感激。”

编者按：

鉴于上述情况，本报收到大上海市政府转来的日本总领事馆照会内容。出于两个邻国之间的友好关系，我们中国人应对日本天皇遇刺未遂一事表达适当的情感。标题中“不幸皇帝随后的车厢被

bombed and that the culprit was at once arrested" is based
on this sentiment. The bombing of the carriage following
the Emperor's is not a pleasant affair and consequently it is
said to be unfortunate. Had the Japanese Emperor been
bombed, the word "unfortunate" would not have been adequate
to describe the case. This paper had no intention of
insulting the Emperor of Japan, on the contrary it expressed
a slight expression of regret in the article in question.
This article must have been misapprehended or misinterpreted
by the staff of the Japanese Consulate who only know part of
the Chinese language and this has resulted in the demands
from the Japanese Consul-General. For this reason, we
do not know how to make the correction and as to the demands
for apology and punishment, it is absolutely unreasonable.
The Chinese have so far never committed any improper acts
in newspapers in the Orient to exasperate the feelings of
people of foreign countries. There are newspapers in
the world which are deliberately arousing the indignation
of the Chinese authorities. We regret this matter very
much. We tender appropriate thanks to the Japanese Consul-
General for his manner of action.

Bulletin issued by the Japanese Press Union
regarding a Chinese Press Report in the Min Kuo Jih Pao.

CONSUL-GENERAL MURAI PROTESTS AGAINST INDISCREET PRESS REPORT

Shanghai, Jan.11.

Mr. Kuramatsu Murai, Japanese Consul-General in
Shanghai, yesterday despatched to Mr. Wu Tieh-cheng, Mayor
of Greater Shanghai, a Note protesting against certain in-
discreet and disrespectful phrase appearing in Jan. 9th issue
of the Minkuo Jihpao, a local vernacular and a well known
Kuomintang official organ.

The article in question related to the cable news
from Tokyo concerning the attempt made upon the life of H.I.M.
the Emperor of Japan by a Korean youth named Li, which took
place on Jan. 8. The Minkuo Jihpao in publishing this cable
report captioned it with the following headlines:
Sh. 70. 8632/8^a. || "Korean Assassin/Makes Attempts on Life of Japanese Emperor.
"UNFORTUNATELY Bomb Explodes Near One of Carriages
Not Carrying Ruler; Korean Captured on Spot".

In his Note, Consul-General Kuramatsu states
that the headlines appearing in the paper show extreme dis-
respect to the Japanese Emperor, and "may be considered as an
intentional attempt on the part of the paper to stimulate anti
Japanese feelings". The Consul-General requests that Mayor
Wu use his influence to let the paper make necessary corrections
and to take other appropriate steps to prevent the Minkuo Jihpao
or any other Chinese paper in the future from publishing such
indiscreet articles.

The phrase in question has considerably aroused the
anger of the local Japanese residents, who believe that the
Kuomintang organ has deliberately used this term to insult the
Japanese sovereign and the Japanese nation, and are demanding
that stern measures be taken to reprimand the editor of the paper.
--Press Union

村井总领事抗议轻率的新闻报道

上海，1月11日。

驻上海日本总领事村井仓松先生昨日向大上海市长吴铁城先生发出照会，抗议1月9日出版的当地白话文报纸、著名的国民党官方机关报《民国日报》中出现的某些轻率且不敬的措辞。

有关文章涉及来自东京的电讯新闻，内容是关于1月8日一名姓李的朝鲜青年企图刺杀日本天皇陛下未遂一事。《民国日报》在刊登此电讯报道时，使用了以下标题：
Sh. 70. 8632/8^a. || “朝鲜刺客/企图刺杀日本天皇。
“不幸炸弹在未载君主的其中一节车厢附近爆炸；朝鲜人当场被捕”。

村井总领事在照会中指出，该报出现的标题显示了对日本天皇的极度不敬，并且“可被视为该报故意试图激起反日情绪”。总领事请求吴市长运用其影响力，让该报进行必要的更正，并采取其他适当措施，防止《民国日报》或任何其他中文报纸今后发表此类轻率的文章。

有关措辞极大地激怒了当地日本居民，他们认为该国民党机关报故意使用这一术语来侮辱日本君主和日本民族，并要求采取严厉措施斥责该报编辑。——新闻联合会

-----
The Min Kuc Pao And The Attempt On The Mikado
The Min Kuo Pao publishes the following
report on January 12, 1932 :-
The Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai
yesterday sent the following letter to the Municipality
of Greater Shanghai :-
"On January 9 the Min Kuo Pao published
an article bearing on an incident which occurred in
Tokyo on January 8 and beneath the heading "Attempted
Assassination of Japanese Emperor by a Korean," the
paper inserted a small heading: "It is unfortunate
that the carriage following the Emperor was bombed
and that the culprit was at once arrested."

《民国报》与针对天皇的袭击
《民国报》于1932年1月12日发布如下报道：
驻上海日本总领事昨日致函大上海市政府：
“1月9日，《民国报》刊登了一篇关于1月8日发生在东京的事件的文章，并在‘朝鲜人企图刺杀日本天皇’的标题下，该报插入了一行小标题：‘不幸皇帝随后的车厢被炸，罪犯随即被捕。’”
